defence_layers_observed: Layer 1 — Cache::lock('fiscal_seq_b{branchId}', 5s TTL) with block(3s) max wait, per-branch serialisation
Layer 2 — DB::transaction wrapping the SELECT MAX / + 1 / INSERT path
Layer 3 — Order::lockForUpdate() on rows of the same branch (row-level DB lock, MySQL InnoDB)
Layer 4 — withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope) + withTrashed() so soft-deleted rows are still considered in MAX(fiscal_sequence_no) — closing the LOCK_FISCAL_WGS_Z6_P1_2026-05-19 hole

race_condition_paths_considered.path: cache outage / split-brain — two workers slip past empty cache
race_condition_paths_considered.mitigation: Layer 2+3 — DB transaction + lockForUpdate serialise at storage engine

race_condition_paths_considered.path: cache lock expires under load mid-transaction
race_condition_paths_considered.mitigation: DB transaction holds storage-level lock until commit; cache lock is correctness optimisation, not the ultimate gate
withTrashed() includes soft-deleted in MAX() — exactly the Z6-P1 LOCK exception scope

race_condition_paths_considered.path: BranchScope hides an existing row with higher fsn
race_condition_paths_considered.mitigation: withoutGlobalScope(BranchScope) makes the MAX scope explicit

ansible_grant_revoke_truncate.mysql_semantic: TRUNCATE requires DROP privilege at the table level. Revoking DROP transitively blocks TRUNCATE. Confirmed in MySQL 8.0 documentation (TRUNCATE TABLE Statement: 'TRUNCATE TABLE requires the DROP privilege')
ansible_grant_revoke_truncate.verdict: CONFIRMED — TRUNCATE bypass on audit_logs/z_reports is blocked by privilege revocation. Defense-in-depth complemented by BEFORE DELETE triggers (DELETE not revoked because app needs row-level delete for soft-delete and GDPR retraction)
